title: x-yaml-dsl-functions
description: A DSL's function table: each function name maps to its description, its arguments in call order and what it returns, or, for a macro, what its preprocessor does with a call.

description.description: What the function does, in markdown.

arguments.description: The function's arguments in call order. Optional arguments follow required ones, and a repeated argument is last.

description.description: What the argument holds, in markdown.

return.description: What the function returns. Left out for a function that returns nothing, and for a macro.

description.description: What the returned value holds, in markdown.

macro.description: Present only on a macro: what the DSL's preprocessor does with a call.

callee.description: On a function_call macro, required: the argument naming the macro or function called.

callee_arguments.description: On a function_call macro: the argument holding the callee's arguments by name.

content.description: On a merge macro, required: the argument holding the content or its location.

loop_variable.description: On a loop macro, required: the argument naming the loop variable.

collection.description: On a loop macro, required: the argument holding the collection.

body.description: On a loop macro, required: the argument holding the body.

name_suffix_pattern.description: The regular expression of the text after the macro's name that keeps sibling calls distinct. Left out, nothing follows the name.

unmarked_key_paths.description: The JSONPaths of the keys that call the macro without the call marker. Left out, none.

merge_behavior.description: How a merge macro combines the holding map with its content. Required on a merge macro.

argumentList.description: Deprecated: use a mapping with description and arguments. The function's arguments in call order.

required.description: Whether a call must pass the argument.

repeated.description: Whether the argument takes every remaining value.

valueType.description: The kind of value; `function` and `macro` are the name of a table entry of that kind.
